items.a: A **terminal and multiplexer in one**, built on the **Ghostty core**, where the server treats the terminal as **just a plug-in**.

items.q: What does merging terminal and multiplexer give users?
items.a: **Persistent sessions** you can reopen from a **phone or another OS**, without a separate tmux layer.

items.q: How is Ghostty's core kept open?
items.a: It sits in a **501(c)(3) non-profit**, and Rex's improvements go **back upstream**.
**Agentic coding tools** like Claude Code: a **simple programming model** and **broad system access** with little sandboxing.

items.q: What does Hashimoto think most agent users really want?
items.a: **Not a terminal**: Rex aims to let them run agents **without realising a terminal is there**.

items.q: What is Hashimoto's rule for UI in Rex?
items.a: **No button without an API**: every element is **API-driven** so agents and scripts can drive it, not bolted on via accessibility.

items.q: What slows the first 100 ms of a macOS app launch?
items.a: **Dynamic linking** and **Gatekeeper certificate checks**, before any of your code runs.

items.q: How will Ghostty hide the ~300 ms Metal context cost?
items.a: By **CPU-rendering the first frames** while acquiring the **GPU context off the main thread**, then switching.

items.q: What is Casey Muratori's Windows startup tip?
items.a: Keep the **startup memory footprint tiny**, because **mapping fresh pages is slow**, and grow it in the background.
